questions.q: What does Invoke-MeridianBackups.ps1 do after the full and log backups complete?
options: It nothing further — a completed Backup-DbaDatabase call is considered sufficient on its own
It calls Test-DbaLastBackup to prove the full backup is actually restorable
It immediately deletes the previous night's backup file
It emails the backup file to Priya for manual review
questions.explain: Following the same principle from Lesson 1, the script proves the backup is genuinely usable with Test-DbaLastBackup rather than just assuming a completed backup command means a good backup.

questions.q: Why does Invoke-MeridianBackups.ps1 wrap its work in try/catch and call Send-MeridianAlert on failure?
options: try/catch is required syntax for every PowerShell function regardless of purpose
Because Backup-DbaDatabase cannot run without being inside a try block
To make the script run faster
So a failed backup gets reported immediately instead of only being discovered the next time someone needs a restore
questions.explain: A silent backup failure is exactly the kind of problem that stays invisible until a restore is actually needed — error handling surfaces it immediately instead.

questions.q: What three facts does Invoke-MeridianHealthCheck.ps1 gather to replace Priya's 40-minute manual routine?
options: CPU temperature, network latency, and Windows Update status
Low disk volumes, last backup success, and failed Agent jobs from the past day
Total row counts for every table in MeridianCommerce
The number of open SSMS windows and active RDP sessions
questions.explain: The script mirrors exactly what Priya used to check by hand: disk space, last night's backup, and any Agent job failures — collapsed into one object and one alert.

questions.q: What does Invoke-DbaDbIndexOptimize decide on a per-index basis?
options: Whether to reorganize, rebuild, or just update statistics, based on fragmentation
Whether to drop the index permanently
Whether to move the index to a different database
Whether to convert the index to a columnstore index
questions.explain: Invoke-DbaDbIndexOptimize inspects fragmentation and statistics for each index and chooses the appropriate maintenance action, the same kind of smart logic DBAs used to hand-roll themselves.

questions.q: Why does Invoke-MeridianIndexMaintenance.ps1 run weekly off-hours rather than nightly like the backup script?
options: dbatools only permits index maintenance commands to run once per week
Weekly is simply the default and cannot be changed
Index maintenance is real I/O and CPU load, and MeridianCommerce's storefront traffic pattern can't absorb that load during the day
Index maintenance produces no load at all, so the schedule doesn't matter
questions.explain: Unlike a lightweight backup, index/statistics maintenance is resource-intensive, so it's scheduled less often and off-hours to avoid affecting the live storefront.
